subject.title: [Bug]: Terminal provider model_not_available in subagent announce path can trigger chat.history storm and gateway event-loop starvation

question: Should this broader report stay as the canonical tracker for terminal provider-error driven subagent announce/history starvation, or should maintainers split it across the existing provider/config and subagent-wake issues?
rationale: The source evidence shows real overlapping gaps, but the safest fix crosses provider classification, fallback semantics, config validation, subagent delivery, and gateway availability policy; automation should not choose that product boundary.

options.title: Keep This Broad Tracker
options.body: Use this issue to coordinate the combined provider-error, announce retry, chat.history pressure, and gateway-starvation acceptance criteria.

options.title: Split To Existing Canonicals
options.body: Move provider/config validation to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/84212 and parent-wake delivery to https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/90178, then close this only after preserving the starvation evidence there.

options.title: Queue A Narrow Classifier Fix
options.body: Treat only the `Model not available` wording as a small provider classifier bug and leave announce/history starvation for separate issues.

recommendation.title: Keep This Broad Tracker
recommendation.body: Use this issue to coordinate the combined provider-error, announce retry, chat.history pressure, and gateway-starvation acceptance criteria.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger is the strongest current-history signal across the relevant subagent and provider-error files in this checkout.
